source.title: GRAWA: Gradient-based Weighted Averaging for Distributed Training of Deep Learning Models

record.tranche_reason: Measures correlations between gradient norm and generalization gap, and reports generalization-gap results for distributed training optimizers. It does not test a listed version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: Gradient norm is measured on 162 trained ResNet-18 models and related to the generalization gap; the reported figure gives no extractable numerical values. Appendix D reports generalization gaps for three model-dataset settings across six distributed optimizers. Cited results on flatness and generalization are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization relationship to design distributed optimizers. Its gradient-norm correlation and unscaled Hessian-norm comparisons do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Optimizer comparisons use SGD-based methods under fixed training time, without testing adaptive optimizers or a fixed-epoch batch-size contrast. No listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors report a positive gradient-norm–gap association and claim faster convergence, generally lower test errors, flatter minima, and reduced communication for GRAWA. These advantages are not universal across comparisons. LGRAWA has the smallest mean gap in each displayed gap-table setting; the table selectively excludes cases where gap approximately equals test error.
record.recipe_differences: Tests gradient-norm correlation and distributed-training algorithms; it does not use the listed versions' recipes or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Gradient norm and generalization gap vary across trained models with different hyperparameters and architectures; the reported gap also varies by optimizer, model, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 162 EASGD-trained ResNet variants on CIFAR-10 without augmentation, the authors report that larger whole-training-set gradient norms accompany larger generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-model gradient norm is associated with generalization gap across the tested hyperparameter and architecture settings.

fits_no_version.finding: LGRAWA has the smallest mean generalization gap in each of the three displayed model–dataset settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distributed optimizer choice affects generalization gap in the reported time-constrained experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1–2 show that lower unscaled Hessian Frobenius norm does not uniformly accompany lower test error; for VGG-16, DP+SAM has norm 134.81 versus LGRAWA's 227.03, but test error 8.92% versus 7.52%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian norm does not consistently rank test error across these distributed optimizers under fixed training-time budgets.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2024)
record.problems: The gradient-norm relation is shown in a figure without a reported numerical correlation or uncertainty. The gap table reports only selected cases and omits other results where the gap equals or is very close to test error. No listed claim version is tested directly.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The paper reports other test-error results and Hessian-norm flatness proxies, but these do not measure one of the listed versions' named outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning conditions and recovery interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Varying batch size in a search grid does not supply this comparison.
Dropout effects, small-data failures, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gap among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: R2–R19 reproduce the supplied gap table correctly but report method performance outside all listed versions. Their shared conditions should include fixed training-time budgets and data augmentation. Hessian results and other test errors are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries. No numerical correlation or uncertainty is reported for R1.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 models (162 models; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated final-model gradient norm with generalization gap (test error minus train error).
rows.measure: Relation between gradient norm and generalization gap; figure only, no numerical correlation reported.
rows.value: Figure 2 shows standardized gradient norms in log scale versus generalization gap; text says gradient norm increases as the gap increases.
rows.note: Study reports an aggregate relation over 162 models, not separate model-level values.
rows.check: The reported gradient-norm association is observed, but cannot establish any listed version. Gradient norm is not magnitude-aware sharpness. Add EASGD training and whole-training-set gradient evaluation to the conditions.
